title: Measuring Verifier Impact in an LLM Generate→Verify→Repair Loop for Intent→Configuration NetOps Tasks
abstract: We measure how inserting a deterministic network verifier into a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) loop affects verifier-detected safety violations for LLM-produced device-configuration proposals. In a preregistered paired design (N = 500 intent→configuration tasks stratified across VLAN-change, ACL-change, and static-route-change clusters) we compared: (1) baseline — a single LLM proposal produced once per task, and (2) guarded — the identical shared LLM proposal validated by a deterministic netops verifier and subjected to up to one automated repair iteration if the verifier flagged a preregistered high/medium-severity violation. Primary outcome: verifier pass (no preregistered high/medium-severity violations). Results (complete pairs = 500): baseline passed 499/500 (0.998), guarded passed 500/500 (1.000); contingency: n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). The preregistered exact McNemar two-sided test was implemented as an exact binomial on discordant pairs (n = n10 + n01) with two-sided p computed as p_two-sided = 2 × min{P(X ≤ n10), P(X ≥ n10)} for X ∼ Binomial(n, 0.5), truncated at 1.0; for the observed discordant counts this yields p = 1.00 under the archived convention. Interpretation: on this verifier-scoped synthetic corpus and model+validator pairing the LLM produced near-ceiling proposals; measured marginal verifier+repair effect on the pass-rate metric is therefore small, though the verifier corrected at least one concrete baseline failure. All preregistration, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call traces, execution logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle for deterministic re-inspection.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in NetOps for intent-to-configuration translation, change planning, and automated repair. Prior systems and surveys emphasize that operational reliability is determined by surrounding engineering—deterministic validators, sandbox replay, canarying, and rollback—rather than model output alone [Beckett et al., 2017; Wei et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. The generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) pattern is frequently proposed: an LLM generates a candidate, a deterministic verifier checks formalized properties, and repairs (automated or human-mediated) are applied for violations. Despite conceptual consensus, controlled measurements that isolate the marginal contribution of a verifier—holding the model’s proposal fixed—are limited. Practitioners need to know: when an LLM already produces high-quality candidates, how much incremental safety does adding a deterministic verifier plus a modest automated repair budget produce on a verifier-scoped pass/fail metric? We preregistered and executed a paired experiment designed to isolate that marginal effect under canonical deterministic semantics.
sections.related_work: Formal, deterministic network-verification approaches (header-space analysis, route-model verifiers, Batfish-style analyzers) can check reachability/isolation and update-atomicity and have informed verifier-in-the-loop designs for NetOps correctness [Beckett et al., 2017]. Concurrent NetOps/AIOps research integrates LLMs for intent parsing and configuration generation while advocating guardrails (e.g., INTA, Confucius, other agentic frameworks) and generate–verify–repair patterns to reduce unsafe outputs [Wei et al., 2025; Wang et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. Work on LLM failure modes (hallucination, overconfidence, tool-integration errors) motivates verifiers and human oversight as mitigations [Owen, 2026; DeepSeek-AI, 2025]. However, public controlled ablations that quantify a deterministic verifier’s marginal effect—keeping the same initial LLM proposal for both conditions—are scarce in the supplied literature. Our artifact-backed paired measurement provides a concrete, reproducible data point in this gap.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory plan. We preregistered study_id cand_7f4b9a2d_hosted_gvr_v1_2026 and froze the research question, task generator seeds, inclusion/exclusion rules, estimands, multiplicity plan, retry policy, and stopping rule before observing outcomes. Primary hypothesis: an LLM paired with a deterministic verifier plus a single automated repair iteration will produce a lower verifier-detected safety-violation rate than the same LLM producing a single proposal without verifier feedback (paired within-task). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline where success == verifier reports zero preregistered high/medium-severity violations. The preregistration and artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle (preregistration SHA-256 recorded in the execution manifest).

Task generator and strata. A deterministic synthetic corpus of 500 intent→configuration tasks was created with deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 using preregistered seeds. Tasks were stratified per the preregistration into VLAN-change = 167, ACL-change = 167, and static-route-change = 166; execution logs and the task manifest confirm that the realized per-cluster composition matched the preregistered allocation and no confirmatory exclusions occurred (complete_pair_count = 500). The generator constrained allowed_features to {admin, mtu, vlan} to match the deterministic verifier’s modeled scope; full task payloads and expected_final_state entries are archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl.

Generation semantics, model, and verifier. To isolate verifier marginal effect we used generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate": for each task the pipeline produced one shared LLM proposal that served as the baseline proposal and was also validated by the guarded arm. The guarded arm invoked an automated single-repair call only if the deterministic verifier reported a preregistered high/medium-severity violation on that shared candidate. Requested LLM = gpt-5-mini via the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter (execution/model_configuration.json); verifier = deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator-spec and violation-severity mapping archived). Repair budget per preregistration: at most one automated repair iteration per pair.

Primary statistical test and implementation. The preregistered confirmatory test was an exact McNemar two-sided test on paired binary outcomes. The archived executor implements the exact two-sided McNemar by: let n = n10 + n01 (discordant pairs) and compute p_two-sided = 2 × min{P(X ≤ n10), P(X ≥ n10)} where X ∼ Binomial(n, 0.5), truncated at 1.0. This is the exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention used by the analysis executor; the archive contains the implementation and parameters (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CIs for the absolute difference were computed with B = 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729), resampling pairs with replacement while preserving pairing.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary outcomes. The run completed with complete_pair_count = 500 and model_calls_used = 501 (shared_initial_generation = 500; repair-stage calls = 1). Aggregated per-condition counts (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes = 499, baseline failures = 1 (baseline_success_rate = 0.998); guarded successes = 500, guarded failures = 0 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Paired contingency (guarded × baseline): n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002.

Exact test and CI. Under the archived exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention this discordant pattern (n = 1, n10 = 1) yields two-sided p = 1.00 (the executor computes p_two-sided = 2 × min{P(X ≤ 1), P(X ≥ 1)} for X ∼ Binomial(1, 0.5) and truncates at 1.0); the paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute difference is [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). Analysis artifacts and logs (analysis/results.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl) record these computations and parameters.

Repair activity and discordant episode provenance. Observed repair-stage provider calls = 1; that single repair produced the sole discordant outcome (n10 = 1): the guarded arm converted one baseline-detected preregistered high/medium-severity violation into a verified pass. The exact per-pair identifier and complete validator_trace and repair-provider-trace for that episode are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl and the provider-call traces; the evidence bundle therefore allows deterministic retrieval of the pair identifier and the full diagnostic/repair transcript by filtering execution/raw_results.jsonl for pairs where baseline scoring indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation and guarded scoring indicates a pass. Execution and reconciliation manifests confirm exactly one such episode and that model_calls_used = 501 and repair-stage calls = 1 are consistent across artifacts.

Power and ceiling effect. The preregistration assumed baseline error prevalence ≈ 0.30 for power planning (N ≈ 384 for 80% power to detect a 10%-point absolute reduction). Observed baseline failure prevalence (1/500) was far lower, producing a ceiling effect that reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute improvements; secondary per-violation-class analyses were uninformative because counts were near-zero. Missingness_summary.csv and contamination diagnostics report zero exclusions and no failed episodes.
sections.discussion:
Conditional interpretation. Under the constrained experimental regime—single requested model (gpt-5-mini), shared_initial_candidate semantics, deterministic verifier coverage limited to modeled features (admin, mtu, vlan), and at most one automated repair—the LLM produced near-ceiling correct proposals and the marginal measured pass-rate benefit of verifier+repair on the composite pass/fail metric was small (0.002). This conditional result shows that when baseline proposal quality is very high for the verifier-modeled properties, modest verifier+repair budgets may yield small measurable pass-rate gains even though verifiers can still correct rare concrete failures (as occurred once here).

Design implications for practitioners. (1) Measure baseline proposal error prevalence on representative operational data before allocating repair budget: when verifier-scoped baseline error is extremely low, marginal pass-rate gains per unit cost may be small. (2) Align verifier coverage and severity mapping with operator-critical constraints; our pass==no-high/medium-severity outcome is defined relative to the verifier-spec archived in the bundle. (3) Choose generation semantics consistent with operational priorities: shared-initial semantics minimize model-call overhead and preserve the original proposal for human review, while verifier-guided regeneration or multiple repair iterations could increase final-pass probability at higher model-call cost.

Threats to validity. Internal validity is supported by preregistration, deterministic seeds, and automated replacement rules; no manual adjudication occurred. Construct validity: the pass/fail metric is defined relative to the deterministic verifier’s coverage and severity mapping; properties outside the verifier scope (vendor-specific behaviors, dynamic protocol state) are not evaluated and would not be captured. External validity: single-model testing, synthetic corpus, and limited feature scope limit generalization to production heterogeneity and cross-vendor CLIs. Conclusion validity: observed ceiling effects reduce statistical sensitivity for small absolute improvements; the archived exact two-sided p = 1.00 reflects the exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention and the small discordant count. All artifacts required to reproduce and audit these claims are archived in the evidence bundle.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment (N = 500) isolating the marginal effect of inserting a deterministic verifier plus one automated repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Baseline proposals passed the verifier on 499/500 pairs; the guarded arm passed 500/500 pairs, yielding an absolute improvement of 0.002 (95% CI [0.0, 0.006]; archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 under the run’s exact-binomial convention). The measurement illustrates a ceiling-effect regime: when baseline proposal quality is very high for verifier-modeled properties, measurable marginal pass-rate benefit from a modest verifier+repair budget can be negligible on a composite pass/fail metric, although verifiers can still correct rare failures. We urge practitioners to measure baseline error prevalence, align verifier coverage with critical properties, and select generation/repair semantics consistent with deployment priorities. All preregistration, code, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle for deterministic re-inspection.

limitations: Synthetic, deterministic task corpus limited to features modeled by the deterministic validator; task payloads constrained to allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}. Results do not generalize to unconstrained production intents, cross-vendor CLI heterogeneity, or protocol semantics outside the verifier scope.
Single requested model family (gpt-5-mini requested) and a single validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) — no claim of multi-model or cross-validator generality is made.
Maximum one automated repair iteration was permitted by the preregistration; different repair budgets or iterative regeneration strategies could change measured verifier impact.

Very high baseline pass rate (499/500) created a ceiling effect that limits power to detect small absolute improvements on the pass-rate metric; the archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 reflects the archived exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention and the small discordant count.

The single discordant episode (the sole task where baseline failed and guarded succeeded) and its validator diagnostics and repair-stage trace are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl in the evidence bundle. To inspect it deterministically: filter execution/raw_results.jsonl for pair entries where the baseline scoring outcome indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation (baseline pass == 0) while the guarded scoring outcome indicates pass == 1; because only one such discordant pair exists in the confirmatory set, this lookup returns the single episode and its provider-call traces. The validator violation-code→severity mapping is archived in the execution manifest and validator-spec artifacts in the bundle.
